concept.title: Label Walk-Through, Clinic Style
concept.big_idea: A calm, structured segment in the creator's usual professional setting: three things to check on a kids' mix label, then the Little Joys Nutrimix label read aloud line by line. He quotes what the pack states and nothing else; no health promises.
concept.objective: Attention-stage creative test with this creator. A hypothesis, not a prediction: organic results do not predict paid performance.
why_fit: Creative DNA: Across 20 posts: formats piece to camera (100%); content expert explainer (100%); language english + hindi (80%), hindi (20%); settings clinical (100%); children on camera 75%; product shown 20%; sponsored 10%.

heavy on explainer / piece to camera (100% of posts): Talking-to-camera is this creator's default; in Little Joys ads it had LOWER hook rates, so test an opening visual or story beat before the explanation. Caution: Post label is broader than the ad label.

Child visible on screen (75% of posts): Build the brief around the creator's own child in the product's routine moment (breakfast, tiffin, milk time). Caution: Ads: the strongest signal is a child in the FIRST 3 s, which posts cannot show (no timing label).
Attention alignment score 25/100 (AI-labelled posts vs paid-ad hook-rate patterns; organic engagement is not treated as evidence of paid performance).

cta.note: Soft, information-led CTA that fits a consult-style creator.

tone.summary: Calm, measured and reassuring: a clinician explaining something to a parent, not selling to them.
delivery: Pace: slow and even; pause after each quoted label line.
Language: Hindi with English terms; list-based ('teen cheezein') structure.
On camera in his usual professional setting; no influencer-style transitions or slang.
Read label lines verbatim; do not paraphrase them into benefits.
tone.creator_voice_in_profile: The tone is consistently calm, clinical, and professional. He speaks with the measured pace of a doctor explaining a diagnosis or treatment plan to a patient's parent.
tone.catchphrases_in_profile: Wearing a stethoscope on camera; Direct questions addressing common parental fears; Structured, list-based advice; Calm, reassuring delivery
tone.native_in_profile: A sponsored post must feel like a clinical consultation or a myth-busting segment. It should feature the creator in his professional attire, using text overlays to highlight key medical takeaways or product benefits.

avoid.item: Any claim that the product treats, prevents or cures anything, or improves immunity, growth, height, weight, brain development or strength.
avoid.reason: No such claim is verified in the supplied files; several older ads contain them (see restricted claims list).

avoid.item: Any number, percentage, multiplier or vitamin count that is not one of the verified product facts for the chosen product.
avoid.reason: Numeric claims must trace to a fact ID.

avoid.item: Superlatives and exclusivity ("best", "only", "No. 1", "bestseller", "loved by 10 lakh moms").
avoid.reason: Appear in older ad copy but cannot be substantiated from the files.

avoid.item: Comparisons with, or mentions of, other brands or products.
avoid.reason: Competitor kids-nutrition brands appear in several shortlisted creators' sponsored posts; keep the Little Joys video clean of them.

avoid.item: Third-party testing or certification claims (e.g. lab tested, Eurofins).
avoid.reason: Mentioned in ad copy, but certificates are not part of the supplied files.

avoid.item: Scripted taste or eating outcomes ("kids love it", "finishes it in two minutes"). Film real reactions only.
avoid.reason: Outcome claims are unverified; scripted reactions would misrepresent what happened.

avoid.item: "Doctor recommended", "expert approved" or any medical-authority endorsement the creator has not personally confirmed.
avoid.reason: Endorsement must be genuine and disclosed.

avoid.item: Age suitability, serving size or dosage statements unless supplied by Little Joys.
avoid.reason: Not available in the supplied files; left as [[CONFIRM: ...]] placeholders.
Every script ends with a disclosure line; confirm the platform's disclosure label.

avoid.item: Energetic transitions, casual slang or a sales-pitch register (the creator's own profile flags these as out of place).
avoid.reason: Creator-specific (from her/his own profile and posts).

avoid.item: Linking the product to any of the medical topics he normally covers (fever, posture, screen time).
avoid.reason: Creator-specific (from her/his own profile and posts).

avoid.item: Other brands visible in this creator's posts (AI-labelled): Areoveda, Calvin Klein, Lacoste, Little Tummys, Troovy. Do not show or mention any in the Little Joys video.
avoid.reason: Exclusivity and clean-brand framing; verify contracts.

avoid.item: Foreign-feeling styles per profile: High-energy, influencer-style transitions, overly casual slang, or a lack of medical context would feel out of place. A script that reads like a generic advertisement rather than a doctor's recommendation will break trust.
